newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nedcor may buy Mauritius bank stake-sources.
newsitem.headline: Nedcor may buy Mauritius bank stake-sources.

text.p: South African bank Nedcor Ltd is in talks on buying a stake in State Bank of Mauritius Ltd , industry and market sources said on Wednesday.
"There are obviously discussions between these two groups," one industry source said.

State Bank is the Mauritian bourse's second largest firm by market capitalisation with a share capital worth 4.857 billion rupees ($229.3 million). "It is not yet a done deal, they are still in negotiations," one market source said.
A Nedcor spokesman declined to comment. "We do not comment on market rumours," he said.
State Bank is seen by investors as smaller and more dynamic than Mauritius' other major bank Mauritius Commercial Bank (MCB).
In 1996 it posted a profit of 417 million rupees, up from 326 million in 1995, while MCB earned 488 million from 433 million.
Both banks benefit from Mauritian citizens' tendency to put a higher percentage of their earnings in savings accounts than is the case in other African nations.
Time and savings deposits as a percentage of gross domestic product in Mauritius are 69 percent, similar to levels in Asia, compared to just 33 percent in South Africa.

No details on the talks have yet emerged, but one market source said Nedbank could take a 15 to 20 percent stake in the bank, possibly with an eye to cashing in on State Bank's plans to expand into the Indian retail banking sector.
An industry source said Mauritius as a whole was attractive for South African firms looking to spread across the Indian Ocean to the potentially lucrative markets of Asia.
"Mauritius acts as a conduit to places further east," the source said.
State Bank has already said it is looking for a strategic alliance with a suitable partner.
State Bank has a 30 percent market share in Mauritius' banking sector and operates 50 branches. It also has opened branches in Mumbai in India and plans to expand in Madagascar.
State Bank shares were last trading at a new year high of 12.70 rupees, up 0.2 rupees on the day. Nedcor was up 75 cents to 100.50 rand.
